Business Development

How to Check, Analyze, Increase, and Compare Website Traffic

  • Fixwebsite Issues
  • July 10, 2025
  • 1:07 pm
  • No Comments

Most healthcare clinics and small businesses focus on getting more website traffic but overlook a critical truth: traffic is only valuable if you understand it, measure it, and use it to improve outcomes. For example, a medical clinic might see 1,000 monthly visitors but no increase in appointments. A local bakery may get Instagram attention but no website orders. A small law firm might be buried on page 3 of Google without knowing why. This guide explains how to check, analyze, increase, and compare website traffic, using clear examples from healthcare and small business sectors. It also explains how to use tools like Google Analytics, Ubersuggest, SEMrush, and Similarweb to drive measurable results.

Table of Contents

Toggle
  • Why Website Traffic Matters
  • Step 1: How to Check Website Traffic (Own and Competitors’ Sites)
  • Step 2: Analyze Website Traffic
  • Step 3: Increase Website Traffic (Free and Paid Methods)
  • Step 4: Use Website Traffic Tools Effectively
  • Step 5: Compare, Rank, and Improve
  • Creative Strategies to Drive More Traffic
  • FAQs
  • Final Action Plan
  • Ready to Grow Your Website Traffic?

Why Website Traffic Matters

Website traffic is more than just a number. It shows:

  • Who is visiting your site

  • How they found you

  • What they do once they arrive

  • Which pages or actions convert visitors into leads, patients, or sales

For healthcare, traffic can lead to appointment requests, patient education, and increased trust. For small businesses, it can mean more inquiries, online purchases, or local foot traffic.

Understanding traffic is the first step toward improving it.

Step 1: How to Check Website Traffic (Own and Competitors’ Sites)

For your own website, start with Google Analytics. It is one of the most reliable tools to check traffic on website and monitor your website traffic status in real time. Google Analytics provides essential data such as total visits and unique visitors, where those visitors are coming from (Google search, social media, referrals, or ads), which pages they are viewing, bounce rates, time spent on the site, and what conversion actions they are taking — such as booking appointments, making purchases, or submitting contact forms. For example, a dental clinic can use Google Analytics to check if people are finding its page through search terms like “emergency dentist near me” or if new patients are arriving via referral links like Yelp. This ongoing insight into your website traffic status helps you understand what’s working, what’s not, and where you need to improve.

For competitor websites, you cannot access their internal data, but you can estimate it using:

  • Ubersuggest: Reveals keyword traffic, SEO difficulty, top-performing pages, backlinks

  • SEMrush: Provides SEO audits, competitor traffic estimates, keyword rankings say like for  urgent care in Miami  or  dental clinic in houston, paid ad data

  • Similarweb: Shows overall site traffic, audience demographics, and traffic sources

For example, a local florist can check how a competing shop ranks for “wedding bouquets Houston” and how much monthly traffic that keyword brings them.

Step 2: Analyze Website Traffic

Looking at traffic numbers is not enough. Analysis means interpreting the data to find strengths, weaknesses, and opportunities.

Key areas to review:

  • Traffic trends over time (growth, decline, seasonality)

  • Traffic sources and channel mix (are you over-reliant on one source?)

  • User behavior on site (which pages convert or cause people to leave)

  • Comparison to competitors (who is outperforming you, and why?)

For example, a healthcare clinic may have strong organic traffic but weak performance from social media, suggesting a need to expand its outreach. A small business may rank well for some local keywords but lose customers because of slow page load speeds or a poor checkout experience.

Step 3: Increase Website Traffic (Free and Paid Methods)

Free methods:

  • Optimize SEO with local and service-based keywords, such as “family doctor Houston” or “custom cakes Katy”

  • Create blogs, videos, or FAQs answering customer or patient questions

  • Improve website speed, mobile-friendliness, and user experience

  • Claim and optimize local listings, such as Google Business Profile, Yelp, or Zocdoc

Paid methods:

  • Launch Google Ads for local or service-specific keywords

  • Run social media ads with precise audience targeting

  • Invest in sponsored placements on reputable local or industry sites

Paid strategies work best when combined with a solid SEO and content foundation.

Step 4: Use Website Traffic Tools Effectively

Each tool provides specific insights that help you make better decisions.

Google Analytics
Google Analytics is the essential tool for tracking your website’s performance. It shows how many visitors come to your site, where they come from (such as Google search, social media, or referrals), and what they do once they arrive. You can see which pages perform best, how long people stay, and which actions they complete — like submitting an appointment form, making a purchase, or signing up for a newsletter. For example, a medical clinic can use Google Analytics to measure whether its blog on “common flu symptoms” is bringing in organic search traffic or whether patients are arriving from Google Maps. Small businesses can track if their product pages are converting or if visitors are dropping off before checkout. Google Analytics works by adding a tracking code to your site that collects user behavior data, which you can then analyze through its interactive dashboard.

Ubersuggest
Ubersuggest is a user-friendly tool for discovering keyword opportunities, understanding SEO difficulty, and analyzing competitor traffic. You can enter a keyword (like “family doctor near me” or “custom cakes Houston”) or a competitor’s website, and Ubersuggest will show you monthly search volumes, how difficult it is to rank for that keyword, estimated site traffic, and backlink profiles. This helps healthcare providers identify what potential patients are searching for, and small businesses can uncover niche markets or product-specific search trends. Ubersuggest also offers content ideas and suggestions for improving rankings. It works by scanning Google search data, competitor sites, and backlink databases to give you practical, actionable SEO recommendations.

SEMrush
SEMrush is a powerful SEO platform designed for advanced site audits, keyword tracking, competitor research, and backlink analysis. By entering your own site or a competitor’s, you can get detailed reports on organic rankings, keyword positions, paid advertising campaigns, backlink sources, and even technical SEO issues like broken links or slow-loading pages. For example, a dental practice can use SEMrush to see how it ranks for “teeth whitening Houston,” what competitors are doing with paid ads, and where to get high-quality backlinks. Small businesses can track their progress over time, monitor keyword positions, and identify gaps in their content strategy. SEMrush works by crawling search engines, analyzing websites, and compiling large-scale datasets to provide a clear competitive landscape and personalized recommendations.

Similarweb
Similarweb is best for understanding the big-picture view of your competitors and market. It estimates overall traffic levels, breaks down where visitors come from (search, social, direct, referrals), and provides insights into audience demographics, such as location, device type, or engagement patterns. For a healthcare clinic, Similarweb can reveal how a competing practice is getting traffic — for example, whether they rely heavily on organic search or if they’re driving users from social media. For small businesses, Similarweb can show which channels competitors focus on and help identify new marketing opportunities. Similarweb works by aggregating data from web crawlers, public sources, and third-party partnerships, using machine learning models to estimate traffic and engagement metrics.

By combining these tools, you can make data-driven decisions rather than guessing what works.

Step 5: Compare, Rank, and Improve

Regularly monitoring your website traffic rankings helps you measure progress and identify areas for improvement.

For healthcare and small businesses, competition is often local. Comparing your website’s performance against competitors allows you to see:

  • Who ranks better for target keywords

  • Who has stronger backlinks or domain authority

  • Who invests in paid advertising and where

For example, if your small business site receives 2,000 visits per month and a competitor’s site draws 10,000, reviewing their SEO, content strategy, and backlink profile can reveal opportunities for you to improve.

Creative Strategies to Drive More Traffic

  • Offer useful tools, such as BMI calculators, symptom checkers, or event planners

  • Provide downloadable resources like health guides, templates, or checklists

  • Turn customer or patient success stories into blog posts or video testimonials

  • Partner with local businesses or influencers to expand your audience reach

  • Focus on niche authority, such as “allergy clinic for children” or “artisan coffee shop with fair-trade beans”

These strategies not only attract more visitors but also build trust and authority in your space.

FAQs

How can I check website traffic for free?
Google Analytics tracks your own site for free, while Ubersuggest and Similarweb offer free versions for competitor estimates.

What is the best website traffic estimator?
SEMrush provides detailed traffic estimates, competitive analysis, keyword tracking, and SEO audits.

How much traffic does a website need to rank?
Ranking depends on factors like keyword competition, content quality, domain authority, and engagement, not just traffic volume. Focus on steady growth and relevance.

Final Action Plan

  • Install Google Analytics and set up goal tracking

  • Use Ubersuggest, SEMrush, and Similarweb to analyze your keywords and competitors

  • Optimize your website content, speed, and user experience

  • Add paid marketing when ready to scale

  • Monitor rankings monthly and adjust based on performance data
